intro: This unit is about family, friends and getting along. Confucius taught about caring for parents. The Daodejing talks about water, soft and strong.
You will learn how many families get ready for Lunar New Year. You will learn about Qingming. You will meet yin and yang, two sides that fit together.
By the end, you can name ways families show respect. You can tell why water can be strong. You can explain harmony in your own words.
bigQuestion: How do families and friends show respect and get along?

timeline.t: Clean the house before Lunar New Year
Hang red paper with good wishes
Share a family dinner and make dumplings
Visit elders and get red envelopes
Watch lion and dragon dances in Chinatown
In spring, clean graves at Qingming
Watch water wear a stone, one drop at a time
Find ways different friends fit together

write.prompt: Tell or draw: How do families and friends show respect or get along? Use two ideas from this unit, like xiao (Analects, book 2) and harmony (Analects, book 13), or water (Daodejing, chapter 8).

title: Family, Friends and Harmony

chapters.title: Respect at Home and the New Year
chapters.bigQuestion: How do families show respect and love for one another?

story.title: Sweeping Before the New Year
story.kicker: A girl cleans the whole house, and her grandmother tells her why.
paragraphs: It was the day before Lunar New Year. Mei held a broom. She swept the kitchen. She swept the hall. She even swept under the beds.
'Why do we clean so much today?' Mei asked. Her grandmother, Nai Nai, smiled. 'We sweep out the old year,' she said. 'Then the new year starts fresh.'
'And tomorrow,' Nai Nai said, 'we will not sweep at all. We keep the good luck in.' Mei laughed. She hung red paper on the door.
That night the family made dumplings together. Mei folded one carefully for Nai Nai. 'Thank you for teaching me,' she said. Nai Nai gave her a warm hug.
story.think: What does your family do to get ready for a special day?

lessons.title: What Is Xiao?
lessons.mainIdea: Xiao means caring for and respecting parents and grandparents, as Confucius taught.
reading: Confucius taught about xiao. You say it like 'shyow.' It means caring for your parents and grandparents. It means showing them respect.
Confucius said xiao is more than giving food. Even animals get fed. Xiao means caring with a respectful heart.

words.d: caring for and respecting parents and grandparents

look.title: More Than Food
look.text: A student asked about caring for parents. The Master said: people think it means feeding them. But dogs and horses are fed too. Without respect, what is the difference?
look.cite: Analects, book 2, passage 7, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: What does Confucius say xiao needs besides food?

check.q: What does xiao mean?
check.why: Xiao means caring for and respecting parents and grandparents.

check.q: What did Confucius say xiao is more than?
check.why: In Analects 2.7 he says it is more than feeding them.

check.q: What does xiao need, as Confucius taught?
check.why: He taught that respect makes the difference.

lessons.title: Let Them Know Where You Are
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught that caring children tell their parents where they are going.
reading: Confucius gave a simple idea. When your parents are alive, do not go far without telling them. Let them know where you are.
Why? Parents worry about their children. Telling them where you go shows you care. It is one small way to show xiao.

words.d: to feel upset because you think something may be wrong

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a boy by the front door. He has his ball. He calls, 'Mom, I'm going to the park with Leo. I'll be back at five!' His mom waves from the kitchen.
look.prompt: How does the boy show care for his mom?

check.q: What did Confucius say to do before going far?

check.why: Analects 4.19 says to let parents know where you go.

check.q: Why tell parents where you go?
choices: They worry and it shows care
check.why: Telling them shows you care about their worry.

check.q: This small act is one way to show what?
check.why: It is one way to show xiao, care for parents.

lessons.title: Getting Ready
lessons.mainIdea: Before Lunar New Year, many families clean the house and hang red decorations.
reading: Lunar New Year comes in winter, in January or February. It follows the moon's calendar. Many families clean the house before it starts.
They hang red paper with good wishes. Red is a color for good luck in China. Many families also eat a big dinner together on New Year's Eve.

words.d: a new year that follows the moon's calendar, in January or February
about the moon

look.prompt: What do many families do first?

check.why: It follows the moon's calendar and falls in January or February.

check.q: What color is used for good luck?
check.why: Red is a color for good luck in China.

check.q: Why do families clean before New Year?
choices: To start the new year fresh
check.why: Cleaning sweeps out the old year.

lessons.title: Red Envelopes and Dumplings
lessons.mainIdea: At New Year, many families visit elders, share dumplings and give red envelopes.
reading: On New Year's Day, many children visit grandparents and elders. They say good wishes. Elders give them red envelopes with a little money inside.
Many families make dumplings together. The dumplings are shaped like old Chinese money. They stand for a good year ahead.

words.d: a red paper envelope with a gift of money, given at New Year
an older person, like a grandparent

look.prompt: Why is making dumplings together special for a family?

check.why: Elders put a little money inside as a gift.

check.q: Who do many children visit at New Year?
check.why: Visiting elders is a way to show respect.

check.q: What do dumplings stand for?
check.why: Shaped like old money, they stand for a good year.

lessons.title: Dragon and Lion Dances
lessons.mainIdea: Dragon and lion dances fill the streets at New Year, including in Chicago's Chinatown.
reading: At New Year there are lion dances and dragon dances. Dancers move inside a big, bright lion costume. Drums and cymbals play loudly.
Chicago's Chinatown has a Lunar New Year parade. Families come to watch. Many families keep New Year customs, whatever their beliefs.

words.d: a neighborhood where many Chinese American families live and have shops
a line of people marching and dancing through the street

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a street in Chicago's Chinatown. A long dragon made of cloth twists by. Many dancers hold it up on poles. Drums boom. Children clap along the sidewalk.
look.prompt: What might you see and hear at a New Year parade?

check.q: Where is a Lunar New Year parade in Illinois?
check.why: Chicago's Chinatown has a Lunar New Year parade.

check.q: What moves inside a big lion costume?
check.why: Dancers move inside the lion costume.

check.q: Who keeps New Year customs?
check.why: Many families keep these customs, whatever their beliefs.

lessons.title: Qingming, Tomb-Sweeping Day
lessons.mainIdea: At Qingming in spring, many families visit graves to clean them and remember ancestors.
reading: Qingming comes in early April. It is also called Tomb-Sweeping Day. Many families visit the graves of their ancestors. Ancestors are family members who lived before us.
Families clean the graves. They bring flowers and food. Some burn incense. They remember and honor the people in their family.

words.d: a spring day when families clean graves and remember ancestors
a family member who lived long before you

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a quiet hill in spring. A family pulls weeds by a grave. A girl sets down fresh flowers. Her father bows gently. The family is quiet and calm.
look.prompt: How is this family showing respect?

check.q: What is another name for Qingming?
check.why: Qingming is also called Tomb-Sweeping Day.

check.q: What is an ancestor?
choices: A family member who lived long before you
check.why: Ancestors are family members from long ago.

check.q: When does Qingming come?
check.why: Qingming comes in early April.

lessons.title: Respect at Home
lessons.mainIdea: Many families show respect at home with kind words, help and a cheerful face.
reading: Confucius said a cheerful face matters when caring for parents. Doing chores is good. Doing them kindly is even better.
Families in many places show respect at home. They greet elders. They help with chores. They listen when others speak.

words.d: a small job at home, like setting the table

check.q: Which is a way to show respect at home?
check.why: Listening shows others that they matter.

chapters.title: Be Like Water
chapters.bigQuestion: How can soft things be strong, and different things fit together?

story.title: One Drop at a Time
story.kicker: A tiny drop of water falls on the same stone every day.
paragraphs: High on a cave roof, a drop of water formed. Drip! It fell onto a big gray stone below. The stone did not move. It was very hard.
The next day, another drop fell. Drip! Then another, and another. Every day, for years and years, drops fell on the same spot.
The stone was hard. The water was soft. But the water never stopped. Slowly, slowly, the stone began to change. No one could see it yet.
One day a child came into the cave with a flashlight. She looked at the stone. There was a small, round hole in it! The soft water had made it, one drop at a time.
story.think: How could something soft like water make a hole in hard stone?

lessons.title: Water Helps Everything
lessons.mainIdea: The Daodejing says the best way to be is like water, which helps everything.
reading: The Daodejing talks about water. It says the best way to be is like water. Water helps all living things. Plants and animals need it.
Water does not fight to be on top. It flows to low places. The Daodejing says this is like the Dao, the Way.

words.d: in the Daodejing, a picture of being soft, helpful and humble

look.title: Like Water
look.text: The best way to be is like water. Water helps all things and does not fight. It goes to the low places others do not want.
look.cite: Daodejing, chapter 8, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1891)
look.prompt: What are two ways water helps living things?

check.q: What does the Daodejing say the best way to be is like?
check.why: Daodejing chapter 8 says the best is like water.

check.q: Where does water flow?
check.why: Water flows down to low places.

check.q: What does water do for living things?
check.why: The Daodejing says water helps all things.

lessons.title: Soft Can Be Strong
lessons.mainIdea: The Daodejing says nothing is softer than water, yet it can wear away hard things.
reading: Water is soft. You can put your hand in it. But the Daodejing says nothing is better at wearing away hard things.
There is a Chinese saying: dripping water wears through stone. It means small steps, done again and again, can do big things.

words.d: easy to press or move; not hard
able to do hard things or last a long time

look.title: Soft and Strong
look.text: Nothing in the world is softer than water. Yet for wearing away hard, strong things, nothing does better.
look.cite: Daodejing, chapter 78, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1891)
look.prompt: How does the cave story show this idea?

check.q: What does the Daodejing say about water?
choices: It is soft but can wear away hard things
check.why: Daodejing 78 says water is soft yet wears away hard things.

check.q: What does 'dripping water wears through stone' mean?
choices: Small steps again and again can do big things
check.why: The saying means steady small steps add up.

check.q: Which is soft?
check.why: Water is soft; you can put your hand in it.

lessons.title: Two Sides That Fit
lessons.mainIdea: Yin and yang are two sides that fit together, like night and day.
reading: Chinese thinkers used two words: yin and yang. Yin is like the shady side of a hill. Yang is like the sunny side.
Yin and yang are different. But they fit together. You need both. Night and day make one whole day.

words.d: two different sides that fit together, like night and day

look.cite: Common examples of yin and yang in Chinese thought
look.prompt: Can you name another pair that fits together?

check.q: What are yin and yang?
check.why: Yin and yang are different sides that fit together.

check.q: Which pair is like yin and yang?
check.why: Night and day are different but fit together.

check.q: What is yang like?

check.why: Yang is like the sunny side.

lessons.title: The Round Symbol
lessons.mainIdea: A round symbol shows yin and yang as dark and light swirling together.
reading: Many people know a round symbol for yin and yang. One half is dark. One half is light. They curl around each other.
Look closely. The dark half has a small light dot. The light half has a small dark dot. Each side holds a bit of the other.

words.d: a picture that stands for an idea

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a circle. Inside, a dark shape and a light shape swirl like two fish. The dark one has a light dot for an eye. The light one has a dark dot.
look.prompt: Why do you think each side has a dot of the other color?

check.q: What does the round yin-yang symbol show?
check.why: It shows dark and light curling together.

check.q: What is inside the dark half?
check.why: The dark half holds a small light dot.

check.q: What is a symbol?
choices: A picture that stands for an idea
check.why: A symbol is a picture that stands for an idea.

lessons.title: Bamboo Bends
lessons.mainIdea: Bamboo bends in the wind and does not break, a favorite picture in Chinese art.
reading: Bamboo is a tall plant. When the wind blows hard, it bends. When the wind stops, it stands up again.
Chinese painters and poets often praised bamboo. Many saw it as a picture of staying calm. It bends but does not break.

words.d: a tall, hollow plant that bends in the wind
quiet and steady inside

look.title: A Picture in Words
look.text: Look at a bamboo grove in a storm. The wind howls. The tall stalks bend low. Leaves shake. Then the wind stops. One by one, the stalks stand tall again.
look.prompt: How is bending in the wind like staying calm?

check.q: What does bamboo do in strong wind?
check.why: Bamboo bends in the wind and stands up again.

check.q: Who often praised bamboo in China?
check.why: Chinese painters and poets often praised bamboo.

check.q: What does calm mean?
check.why: Calm means quiet and steady inside.

lessons.title: Harmony with Friends
lessons.mainIdea: Confucius taught that good people get along with others without making everyone the same.
reading: Harmony means getting along well. Think of a song. Many different notes play together. They sound good as one.
Confucius said a good person lives in harmony with others. But not everyone has to be the same. Different friends can fit together.

words.d: getting along well, like different notes in one song

look.title: Harmony, Not Sameness
look.text: A good person gets along with others but does not make everyone the same. A small person makes everyone the same but does not get along.
look.cite: Analects, book 13, passage 23, retold simply from James Legge's translation (1861)
look.prompt: How can friends who are different still get along?

check.q: What does harmony mean?
check.why: Harmony means getting along well together.

check.why: Analects 13.23 says harmony does not mean sameness.

check.q: How is harmony like a song?
check.why: Many different notes can sound good as one.
